newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up on bargain hunting.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were firmer late afternoon late afternoon on Friday on bargain hunting as the market found a new support level amid scattered demand from China, traders said.
"The demand is there and now the buyers are coming out because prices have fallen a lot," one trader.
"I think prices should not have gone under $22.00 in the first place," another trader said.
July paper was last quoted at $22.30/$22.40 per barrel, up from late Wednesday's $21.95/$22.05, brokers said. August was quoted at $22.75-$22.85, up from Thursday's $22.55/$22.65, they said.
As a result of the renewed confidence in the front month, the July/August time spread as narrowed from minus 60 cents to minus 50 cents, the brokers said.

Traders attributed the firmer prices to bargain hunting as well as new demand from China and expectations that the physical market will consolidate at around the $22.00-per-barrel mark after trading earlier this week at $21.45 and $21.60 per barrel.
China is said to have bought at least three cargoes over the past week--one from Singapore and two from Northeast Asia--to take advantage of the low prices.
China's scattered interest came about despite concerns that China might continue to clamp down on imports due to the high stocks and to encourage endusers to buy oil products from local refineries.
July swaps traded at a low of $21.60 earlier this week after a new round of physical sellers pushed cash prices down to a traded 20-month low of $21.45 per barrel free-on-board Singapore.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade remain wide with both July and August bid 10 cents higher from Thursday at about $1.10 per barrel, brokers said, despite the rebound in gas oil prices.
The firm jet fuel values were attributed to talk that Indonesia's July requirements could be more than two million barrels, from their normal one million barrels.
Fuel oil swaps was last quoted weaker due lower physical trades where a 20,000 tonne cargo traded at $100.00 per tonne, down $1.50 from Thursday.
July was last quoted at $98.00/$98.75 from $98.50/$99.00, brokers said. July traded earlier in the day at $98.10.
